Many myths exist regarding genital warts that may lead to unnecessary anxiety among patients. Some of the myths include:

Myth: Every bump in the genital region is a genital wart.
Fact: There are many other conditions, such as skin tags, molluscum contagiosum, cysts, and others that can look like genital warts.

Myth: People who have genital warts will always experience symptoms.
Fact: There may be minor symptoms in some cases, or people might not notice any symptoms at all.

Myth: Genital warts indicate poor personal hygiene.
Fact: They have nothing to do with hygiene since they are caused by the human papillomavirus.

Myth: Genital warts cannot be treated.
Fact: Several treatment methods effectively eliminate them from the body.

Myth: Patients can identify their condition by themselves.
Fact: It is very important to visit your doctor since many other conditions may be confused with genital warts.

Seeking proper care will help you avoid unnecessary worries and undergo appropriate therapy.

Schedule a consultation with Dr Vedant Ghuse, a trusted dermatologist near me, and get professional help in dealing with any concerns regarding your health issues.

Warts are common skin growths caused by viruses, but DIY wart removal techniques can be dangerous.

There are many remedies advertised on the Internet promising instant effects. Unfortunately, home treatments such as cutting off, burning, tying off, or applying chemical substances can cause infections, scars, damage to your skin, pain, irritation, and incorrect diagnosis of the nature of the skin problem

It’s possible to confuse another type of skin growth with a wart. Moles, skin tags, molluscum contagiosum, and many others can have similar symptoms but need special treatment.

A professional approach to wart removal helps in diagnosing and using tested treatment techniques like cryotherapy, cautery, laser therapy, or any other procedure recommended by a dermatologist.

The main objective of a professional treatment is to remove the growth while ensuring minimal pain and preventing the appearance of warts in the future.

Genital warts are one of the most frequently occurring skin diseases, which are caused by a number of types of HPV viruses. Although the symptoms associated with these warts are not too severe, diagnosis and proper treatment are very important.

Typical signs and symptoms include:

●	Appearance of small, flesh-colored or grey bumps in the genital region
●	Development of groups of bumps, which look like cauliflowers
●	Itching and irritation
●	Irritation when performing routine actions
●	Slow increase in size and number of warts

Sometimes patients cannot distinguish genital warts from benign skin conditions, such as skin tags or ingrown hairs. As a result, the diagnosis becomes late.

The main thing to keep in mind is that any bump in the genital area is not necessarily a sign of warts. A professional examination can identify the exact problem and provide proper treatment.

June is Acne Awareness Month, and it is an opportunity to highlight the fact that acne is not only an aesthetic problem but may cause other issues, such as low self-confidence and poor quality of life, for anyone, regardless of age.

Acne happens when pores get plugged by oil, dead skin cells, and bacteria. Although acne is considered to be typical for young people during their teenage years, adults can also suffer from recurrent breakouts caused by hormonal changes, stress, genetics, and wrong skincare products, among others.

The most common myth about acne is that it does not require immediate action since it will eventually disappear. However, procrastination in treating this problem may lead to additional complications, including scarring and skin discoloration.

There is a range of solutions that can help eliminate acne and even remove acne scars using a modern dermatological approach, which includes medical skincare and prescribed medications, as well as various procedures for acne and acne scars.

In case acne causes discomfort and poor aesthetics of your skin, you should visit Dr Vedant Ghuse, a leading dermatologist near me, to improve the state of your skin.

While dry skin occurs in many people, it can become a medical issue if it is very severe, persistent over time or has other symptoms associated with it. In most normal situations, dry skin will improve with the use of moisturizers after being exposed to dry winter air or by using regular soap.

However, you need to see your doctor if you have the following signs or symptoms:

Continuous flakes that are from flaking skin and have been there a long time
Areas of red or inflamed skin, itching that affects daily functioning
Frequent infections at the site of scratching or bleeding from the area
If the itchy areas have a rash, scaling or thickened skin

You could be suffering from eczema, psoriasis or ichthyosis, and it is important to get evaluated early so that the condition does not worsen, develop complications or develop pigmentation issues.

If you have an itchy rash from eczema or psoriasis, scratching and irritating the skin can worsen dark spots in the summer months.

When you scratch your rash, it can cause damage to your skin and lead to inflammation that triggers the body's response. In individuals with darker skin tones such as Indian skin types, this inflammation creates stimulation for melanin production (dark pigmentation) which contributes to post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation (PIH). PIH are difficult to treat but can take many months to resolve after the original inflammation is treated. UV light exposure worsens this situation by stimulating melanin and leading to increased dark pigmentation in scratched areas.

To avoid developing dark spots, it is best to avoid scratching or irritating the skin, use gentle moisturisers, apply a broad-spectrum sunscreen, and be cautious of indoor UV exposure.

If you are suffering from excessive itching and developing pigmentation this summer, contact Dr. Vedant Ghuse, a trusted dermatologist in Ghatkopar, for an individualised treatment plan to minimise flare-ups and reduce the appearance of dark pigmentation. Schedule an appointment today!

Chronic itching, also known as pruritus, can be related to more than just having dry skin. There may be an underlying cause, such as atopic dermatitis, psoriasis, allergies or systemic conditions.

A visit to a dermatologist may be warranted if you experience any of these:

You have had persistent itching for weeks or months without relief from moisturising.
You develop red, scaly, or thickened patches on your skin.
You have had scratching that has resulted in bleeding, infection, or changed skin pigmentation
Itching interferes with your sleep, job or daily activities.

Getting evaluated early can help determine the cause and appropriate treatment for your chronic itching, which may reduce the risk of future outbreaks, complications and long-term damage to the skin.

Factors affecting the duration that laser treatment will remain effective include: the type of treatment; your skin type; your lifestyle; and how well you care for your skin after treatment. Results from Nd:YAG laser procedures build up over time; however, they can last a long period of time if you follow post-care instructions that reflect proper care for your skin.

Examples of the length of time that improvements in pigmentation and acne scars will last range anywhere from several months to several years. It is critical that you always use sunblock on a daily basis to maintain your results.

In regards to laser hair reduction, the hair follicles that have had laser hair removal performed, permanently reduce their ability to produce hair. As you may have noticed, external factors (ex. hormonal stimulation) can influence hair growth; therefore, continued maintenance treatments may be required periodically to keep your hair removed.

Long-term results are achieved by incorporating medical skin care, sun protection, and regularly scheduled follow-up visits with your clinician, in conjunction with your laser treatments.

The Nd:YAG laser is a desirable option for reducing skin discolourations and improving uneven skin tone through the technique known as laser toning. If you meet any of the following conditions, you may be a suitable candidate for this procedure:

1. You have stubborn pigmentation that has not responded to topical treatments nor improved with home skin care regimens such as creams or serums. These types of abnormal skin pigmentation may have deeper roots within the skin, making them untreatable with topical products designed to penetrate only the superficial layers of the skin.

2. You have brown complexion and are searching for a more effective way to treat stubborn pigmentation. The Nd:YAG laser targets deeper layers of melanin in the skin while also reducing the amount of damage caused by laser therapy in the surface layers of the skin, making Nd:YAG laser therapy a safe alternative for other types of laser therapy for individuals with darker complexions when performed by skilled practitioners.

owner_posts.post_text:
Why Do I Prescribe Melatonin? ⭐
Melatonin is commonly known as the "sleep hormone," but its role extends beyond improving sleep quality.

In selected patients, melatonin may help regulate sleep patterns, support the body's natural circadian rhythm, and contribute to overall well-being. Since poor sleep and chronic stress can influence hair shedding, optimizing sleep is often an important part of a comprehensive hair-loss management plan.

Hair health is not just about what is applied to the scalp—it is also influenced by lifestyle, nutrition, stress, and sleep.

Microneedling for Hair Loss – A Technique We Helped Bring into Mainstream Trichology

Did you know that our team was among the first to publish clinical research demonstrating the benefits of microneedling in androgenetic alopecia?

Our landmark study showed that microneedling can be an effective adjunct to conventional hair loss treatments, opening new possibilities for patients struggling with hair thinning and hair loss.

Years later, microneedling continues to be one of the most widely used procedures in trichology worldwide.

Hair loss treatment is not one-size-fits-all. A detailed scalp evaluation is essential before choosing the right treatment plan.

Pleased to share our recently published work evaluating the effect of combining anthralin with systemic steroids in a patient with alopecia totalis.

Using a unique split-scalp approach, one side of the scalp received anthralin along with systemic steroids, while the other side received systemic steroids alone. 
Authors:
Dr. Rachita Dhurat & Dr. Richa Sharma

How Long Should Hair Loss Medicines Be Continued?

One of the most common questions patients ask is: "When can I stop my hair-loss medicines?"

The answer depends on the cause of hair loss.

For conditions such as androgenetic alopecia (pattern hair loss), treatment often needs to be continued long-term to maintain results. Stopping treatment may lead to gradual loss of the benefits achieved.

Hair-loss treatment is not the same for every patient. The duration and type of treatment should be individualized based on the diagnosis, severity of hair loss, and treatment response.

If you have questions about your hair-loss medications, consult a dermatologist before making any changes.

Barcelona 2026
Delighted to be part of the faculty at the Third Barcelona Hair Meeting, where experts from around the world will come together to share knowledge, research, and clinical experience in hair and scalp disorders.
Looking forward to exchanging ideas, learning from colleagues, and contributing to the evolving science of trichology.

Hands-On Training in Clinical Trichology-Excellence in patient care begins with quality training.

A glimpse from the hands-on component of our Fellowship in Clinical and Procedural Trichology, where delegates receive practical exposure to hair restoration procedures, treatment planning, and real-world clinical decision-making.

Our goal is to bridge the gap between theory and practice through structured mentorship, live demonstrations, and supervised procedural training.

Proud to contribute to advancing trichology education and clinical excellence.

Hair Loss Treatment: Is Oral Minoxidil Necessary?- This is one of the most common concerns I hear from patients with hair loss.

The good news is that treatment for androgenetic alopecia can often be individualized based on the patient's needs, medical history, and preferences.

While minoxidil remains a gold-standard treatment for androgenetic alopecia, several treatment strategies may be considered after a detailed evaluation.

If you are experiencing hair thinning or excessive shedding, consult a dermatologist to understand the most appropriate treatment options for your condition.
Conducted a workshop in regenerative trichology for Raipur dermatologists in May 2026

🎙️ Featured on Vividh Bharati National Service

I recently had the opportunity to discuss common hair problems and hair care practices on the program "Sehatnama" with RJ Yunus Khan.

We spoke about common causes of hair loss, misconceptions surrounding hair care, and the importance of seeking timely dermatological consultation for persistent hair and scalp concerns.

Public education is an important part of improving hair health awareness, and I am grateful for the opportunity to reach a wider audience through this national platform.

owner_posts.post_text:
Not every acne mark is a scar — and the difference decides your treatment.

The red or brown marks left after a breakout are usually post-inflammatory pigmentation, and with the right care they fade. True acne scars — the small depressions in the skin — need a different approach entirely. Treating one as the other wastes months.

That distinction starts with a proper diagnosis by a qualified dermatologist, not a guess. At our Chembur clinic we look at your skin closely, identify exactly what you're dealing with, and build the plan around the marks you actually have — informed by 50 years of documented dermatology behind Dr. Sheth's.

If you've been searching for acne scar treatment in Chembur, you don't need to travel across the city for it. Book a consultation right here and find out what your marks actually are — and what will work.

Hair loss has many causes, and the right treatment depends on identifying which one. At Dr. Sheth's Skin & Hair Clinics in Chembur, Mumbai, hair loss is assessed by qualified dermatologists who look for the underlying cause before recommending treatment. Common causes include genetic patterning (androgenetic alopecia), thyroid and hormonal changes, nutritional deficiencies such as low iron or ferritin, post-illness or postpartum shedding (telogen effluvium), and scalp conditions like dandruff or seborrhoeic dermatitis. Each is treated differently, so a proper diagnosis (medical history, scalp examination and, where needed, blood work) is the first step, not a one-size prescription. Dr. Sheth's has cared for Mumbai's skin and hair for 50 years, and that documented clinical experience now sits in Chembur. If you're noticing thinning, increased shedding or a widening part, an early consultation gives the clearest path forward. Book a hair-loss consultation at our Chembur clinic.

Most people seek treatment for hair loss when thinning becomes clearly visible. By then, the underlying scalp condition — chronic inflammation, seborrhoeic dermatitis, follicular miniaturisation — has often been progressing unaddressed for months.

At Dr. Sheth's Skin & Hair Clinics, we see hair and scalp concerns at every stage: from persistent dandruff and early shedding that does not respond to over-the-counter products, to more advanced thinning that may require procedural treatment such as GFC, PRP, or, where appropriate, a hair transplant carried out in-clinic by a specialist surgeon.

If you have been managing recurring scalp issues or progressive hair loss, a structured dermatologist evaluation is usually more efficient than cycling through products that do not address the root cause.

Our clinic is open Monday through Saturday. New patients begin with a dermatologist consultation — we assess your specific condition before recommending any treatment.

You've probably heard a hundred reasons your hair is thinning. Stress. Diet. Genetics. The shampoo your mother used.
Each could be true. Most of the time, only one is.
At our Chembur clinic, the first thing we do for a hair concern isn't a treatment — it's an evaluation. A scalp examination, a pull test, density assessment. Where it's needed, blood work for thyroid, ferritin, vitamin D. A trichoscope when the eye can't tell the full story.
It sounds clinical. It's actually the difference between a year of treatment that works and a year of treatment that doesn't. Hair loss from genetics looks similar to hair loss from a shedding episode looks similar to a scarring condition. The treatments are not similar at all.
Once we know what we're treating, we can talk about what to do about it — medical management, regenerative therapies like GFC, PRP, exosomes, or a transplant referral when that's the right call.
Start with the evaluation. The plan follows.

Most pigmentation concerns brought to our Chembur clinic have one thing in common: they started small and went unaddressed for too long.

Melasma, sun-triggered marks, and post-inflammatory discolouration all respond better to early, consistent treatment than to periodic intervention once they become pronounced. The difficulty is that over-the-counter products often address the surface without identifying the underlying driver — hormonal shifts, UV exposure, or a compromised skin barrier — which is why the same concern keeps returning.

At Dr. Sheth's Skin & Hair Clinics in Chembur, our dermatologists assess pigmentation at the root level. We build treatment protocols around the cause, not just the appearance — combining medical-grade topicals, procedural options where clinically appropriate, and long-term maintenance suited to your skin.

April is one of the better times to begin. Sun intensity rises through summer, and getting a management plan in place before peak exposure makes a measurable difference.
